title: K-flat replacements within finite filtered module complexes
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A finitely filtered complex means an integer cochain complex $K$ of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with a decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration] and integers $a<b$ such that $F^aK=K$ and $F^bK=0$ as complexes. Write $\operatorname{gr}^iK=F^iK/F^{i+1}K$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. A filtered quasi-isomorphism is a filtered chain map inducing a quasi-isomorphism on each $\operatorname{gr}^i$. Call such a complex good if all modules $K^n,(F^iK)^n,(\operatorname{gr}^iK)^n$ are flat (tensoring with each preserves exact sequences), and all complexes $K,F^iK,\operatorname{gr}^iK$ are K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex].
Every finitely filtered complex $K$ admits a filtered map $P\to K$ which is a quasi-isomorphism on the underlying complex, on every filtration step, and on every graded complex, where $P$ is good, $F^aP=P$, $F^bP=0$, and every module $P^n,(F^iP)^n,(\operatorname{gr}^iP)^n$ is free [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. There is no bound required on the cochain degrees of $P$.
Let $\mathcal H_f(R)$ be the homotopy category of all finitely filtered complexes, where for filtered chain maps $f,g:K\to L$ between finitely filtered complexes a filtration-preserving chain homotopy is a family $h^n:K^n\to L^{n-1}$ satisfying $f-g=dh+hd$ and $h^n(F^iK^n)\subseteq F^iL^{n-1}$, and let $\mathcal G_f(R)$ be its full subcategory of good complexes. Let $W$ denote the filtered quasi-isomorphisms. The inclusion induces an equivalence of localizations
$$\mathcal G_f(R)[W^{-1}]\ \simeq\ \mathcal H_f(R)[W^{-1}].$$
Here localization means formally inverting the indicated maps. Thus comparisons and their equalities may be represented by roofs of filtered chain maps between good complexes. No choice of a functorial free resolution is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0H7X, lemma-resolution-filtered-complex, finite-interval form obtained by replacing its resolution P by F^aP/F^bP; filtered quasi-isomorphisms form a saturated multiplicative system by Derived Categories Tag 05S1, lemma-filtered-acyclic, and their localization is Tag 05S2, definition-filtered-derived. The localization equivalence is the finite filtered resolution/roof formulation of the construction; cache /home/ubuntu/c1-stacks-review/more-algebra.tex and derived.tex.

proof.text:
Fix the bounds $a<b$ of $K$. We construct the resolution using only filtration labels $j\in\{a,\ldots,b-1\}$. Put
$$P_0^n=\bigoplus_{a\leq j<b}\ \bigoplus_{z\in Z^n(F^jK)}R\xi_{j,z},\qquad d_{P_0}=0,$$
let $F^iP_0^n$ be spanned by the generators whose label $j$ satisfies $j\geq i$, and send $\xi_{j,z}$ to $z$. These formulas give a filtered chain map $f_0:P_0\to K$. For $a\leq i<b$ every cycle in $F^iK$ has its generator with label $i$, so $H^n(F^if_0)$ is surjective. For $i\leq a$ use label $a$ and $F^iK=K$; for $i\geq b$ both steps are zero. Thus the underlying cohomology map is also surjective. Each term, step and graded term has the displayed subset of generators as a basis.

source.place: Tag 0H7X, lemma-resolution-filtered-complex, initial basic complex; finite-label adaptation

proof.text: Suppose the filtered chain map $f_m:P_m\to K$ is constructed. For every $a\leq j<b$, integer $n$, and cycle $z\in Z^n(F^jP_m)$ for which $f_m(z)$ is a boundary in $F^jK$, choose $y_{j,z}\in(F^jK)^{n-1}$ with $d_Ky_{j,z}=f_m(z)$. Adjoin a fresh free generator (distinct for every stage and index) $\eta_{m,j,n,z}$ in degree $n-1$ with filtration label $j$, set $d\eta_{m,j,n,z}=z$ and $f_{m+1}(\eta_{m,j,n,z})=y_{j,z}$, and retain all old generators and maps. Since $dz=0$ and $d_Ky_{j,z}=f_m(z)$, the differential squares to zero and $f_{m+1}$ is a chain map. Since $z\in F^jP_m$ and $y_{j,z}\in F^jK$, both preserve the filtration. The inclusions $P_m\subset P_{m+1}$ split on graded modules, on every filtration step and on every associated graded module, by projection onto old generators; their quotient complexes have zero differential and free terms. Every class in the kernel of $H^n(F^jf_m)$ becomes the boundary of its new generator in $F^jP_{m+1}$.

Take $P=\bigcup_{m\geq0}P_m$ with $F^iP=\bigcup_mF^iP_m$ and $f=\bigcup_m f_m$. All generators have labels in $[a,b)$, so $F^aP=P$ and $F^bP=0$. Surjectivity of $H^n(F^if)$ follows from the generators already in $P_0$. For injectivity, a cycle in $F^iP$ has finite support, hence lies in $F^iP_m$ for some $m$ and is a cycle there, since all inclusions are injective. If its image is a boundary in $F^iK$, step 2 makes it a boundary in $F^iP_{m+1}$ (use label $a$ if $i\leq a$; the case $i\geq b$ is zero). Consequently $F^if$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every integer $i$, and $f$ itself is one by taking $i=a$. This argument uses finite support directly and does not assume that $P$ is bounded in cochain degree.

source.place: Tag 0H7X, lemma-resolution-filtered-complex, union and proof of (3); finite-support verification of the colimit argument

proof.text: For every $i$, use the degreewise short exact rows $0\to F^{i+1}P\to F^iP\to\operatorname{gr}^iP\to0$ and the corresponding row for $K$. The long exact sequences [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] and their naturality [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] give a commuting diagram of exact rows $A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{v}C\xrightarrow{w}D\xrightarrow{x}E$ and $A'\xrightarrow{u'}B'\xrightarrow{v'}C'\xrightarrow{w'}D'\xrightarrow{x'}E'$, where the unprimed terms are $H^n(F^{i+1}P),H^n(F^iP),H^n(\operatorname{gr}^iP),H^{n+1}(F^{i+1}P),H^{n+1}(F^iP)$ and the primed terms are those for $K$. Call the vertical maps $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta,\epsilon$; all except $\gamma$ are isomorphisms by step 3. Given $c'\in C'$, choose $d\in D$ with $\delta(d)=w'(c')$. Then $\epsilon(x(d))=x'w'(c')=0$, so $x(d)=0$ and $d=w(c_0)$ for some $c_0\in C$. Now $w'(c'-\gamma(c_0))=0$, so $c'-\gamma(c_0)=v'(b')$. Choose $b$ with $\beta(b)=b'$; then $\gamma(c_0+v(b))=c'$. For injectivity, if $\gamma(c)=0$ then $\delta(w(c))=0$, hence $w(c)=0$ and $c=v(b)$. Since $v'\beta(b)=0$, write $\beta(b)=u'(a')$ and choose $a$ with $\alpha(a)=a'$. Then $\beta(b-u(a))=0$, whence $b=u(a)$ and $c=vu(a)=0$. Therefore $\gamma=H^n(\operatorname{gr}^i f)$ is an isomorphism for every $n,i$.

source.place: Tag 0H7X, lemma-resolution-filtered-complex, proof of (3), graded pieces via short exact sequences; Tag 0117, lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain

proof.text: Each $P^n$ has as a basis all generators adjoined in degree $n$. The subsets with label $j\geq i$ and $j=i$ give bases for $(F^iP)^n$ and $(\operatorname{gr}^iP)^n$, respectively. Free modules are tensor-flat directly: tensoring with $\bigoplus_I R$ gives $\bigoplus_I(-)$, which preserves injections, kernels and surjections by checking the finitely many nonzero coordinates. For each of $C=P,F^iP,\operatorname{gr}^iP$, take $D_0=0$ and $D_{m+1}=P_m,F^iP_m,\operatorname{gr}^iP_m$, respectively. The first quotient $D_1/D_0$ has zero differential and free terms by step 1. For every $m\geq1$, step 2 supplies the degreewise split inclusion $D_m\subseteq D_{m+1}$ and its zero-differential free quotient; step 3 supplies exhaustiveness. [lem-kun-split-cell-complex-kflat] therefore proves K-flatness of each $C$. This proves all the replacement assertions and goodness of $P$, without a cochain-degree bound.

source.place: Tag 0H7X, lemma-resolution-filtered-complex, proofs of (1) and (2); Tags 0BYH and 06Y3

proof.text: By [lem-kun-filtered-quasi-isomorphism-fractions], $W$ in $\mathcal H_f(R)$ has a right calculus of fractions and two-out-of-three. We verify its restriction to the full subcategory $\mathcal G_f(R)$ explicitly. Given $f:X\to Z$ and $s:Y\to Z$ with $s\in W$ and $X,Y,Z$ good, the ambient right Ore axiom gives $t:T\to X$ in $W$ and $g:T\to Y$ with $f\circ t=s\circ g$. Resolve $T$ by $p:P_T\to T$ using steps 1–5. Then $t\circ p:P_T\to X$ belongs to $W$, $g\circ p:P_T\to Y$ is a map between good objects, and $f\circ(t\circ p)=s\circ(g\circ p)$ by associativity. For cancellation, if $f,g:X\to Y$ and $s:Y\to Z$ with $s\in W$ satisfy $s\circ f=s\circ g$ with $X,Y,Z$ good, ambient cancellation gives $t:T\to X$ in $W$ with $f\circ t=g\circ t$. After resolving $T$, the denominator $t\circ p$ lies in $W$ and $f\circ(t\circ p)=g\circ(t\circ p)$. These equations are equations modulo filtration-preserving homotopy, precisely the morphism equality in both full homotopy categories. Identities, composition and two-out-of-three restrict immediately.

source.place: Tags 05S1, lemma-filtered-acyclic, and 05S2, definition-filtered-derived; restriction of the right Ore and cancellation axioms using the constructed resolutions

proof.text: Let $Q_H,Q_G$ be the two localization functors, and $J$ the functor induced by inclusion. For every $K\in\mathcal H_f(R)$, the object $Q_H(K)$ is isomorphic to $JQ_G(P_K)$ through the image of $P_K\to K$ in $W$, so $J$ is essentially surjective. To prove fullness, apply [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation] in $\mathcal H_f(R)$ to a morphism from $Q_H(A)$ to $Q_H(B)$ with $A,B$ good, representing it by $A\xleftarrow{s}T\xrightarrow{u}B$ with $s\in W$. Replace $T$ by $p:P_T\to T$ as above. The roof $A\xleftarrow{sp}P_T\xrightarrow{up}B$ lies entirely in the good subcategory and has the same localized value, since $Q_H(p)$ is invertible. Thus it is the image under $J$ of a morphism in the good localization.

source.place: Tag 04VI, lemma-morphisms-right-localization, singleton case; applied to the filtered localizations of Derived Categories Tag 05S2, definition-filtered-derived.

proof.text: For faithfulness, write two morphisms in the good localization as roofs $A\xleftarrow{s_i}P_i\xrightarrow{u_i}B$ using [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation] and step 6. If their images agree in the ambient localization, [lem-pc-right-fraction-common-refinement] gives $r_i:T\to P_i$ with $s_1r_1=s_2r_2\in W$ and $u_1r_1=u_2r_2$ in the filtered homotopy category. Replace $T$ by $p:P_T\to T$. Then $r_ip$ are morphisms between good complexes, $s_1r_1p=s_2r_2p\in W$, and $u_1r_1p=u_2r_2p$. The same common-refinement criterion, now in the good subcategory, proves equality of the original two morphisms. Hence $J$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective. To construct an inverse, for each ambient localized object $D$ choose a good localized object $V(D)$ and an isomorphism $e_D:J(V(D))\to D$. For an arrow $h:D\to E$, define $V(h)$ as the unique arrow whose image under $J$ is $e_E^{-1}\circ h\circ e_D$. Faithfulness proves the identity and composition laws. The $e_D$ form a natural isomorphism $JV\cong\mathrm{id}$; lifting $e_{J(C)}$ through the same hom-set bijections gives a natural isomorphism $VJ\cong\mathrm{id}$. Thus $J$ is an equivalence. Choosing chain-map representatives for these homotopy classes gives the asserted roofs of filtered chain maps; the equalities of representatives mean filtration-preserving chain homotopies at the refinement. No functorial free resolution was used.
